title: Estátua feminina na abertura da amostra dos produtos do Rio Grande do Sul
creator: José Boscagli (photographer)
description: Black and white photograph showing a female statue displayed at the National Exhibition of 1908. Female allegorical figure representing progress and abundance at the Rio Grande do Sul exhibition pavilion.
citation_abnt: BOSCAGLI, José. [Estátua feminina na abertura da amostra dos produtos do Rio Grande do Sul]. 1908. 1 fotografia, p&b, 16,5 x 23 cm. Museu Histórico Nacional. Disponível em: https://brasilianafotografica.bn.gov.br/brasiliana/handle/20.500.12156.1/11778.
panofsky_pre: B&W photo of female statue at 1908 National Exhibition, RS pavilion. Full body, classical drapery, frontal.
panofsky_funcao: Aesthetic legitimation of republican modernization project

title: Detalhe do monumento à República, Praça da República, Belém
creator: Unknown (Getúlio Vargas visit album)
description: Close-up detail of female allegorical figure holding a flag, standing on a lion. Part of the Monument to the Republic in Praça da República, Belém. The female figure personifies the Brazilian Republic with classical republican iconography — flag, lion (strength), classical garb.
citation_abnt: MONUMENTO à República, Praça da República, Belém. 1940. 1 fotografia, p&b. In: Álbum de fotografias da visita de Getúlio Vargas a Belém. Museu da República/IBRAM. Disponível em: https://brasilianafotografica.bn.gov.br/brasiliana/handle/20.500.12156.1/13609.
panofsky_pre: B&W photo detail, Republic monument Belém. Female on lion holding flag. Low-angle shot from Vargas visit album 1940.
panofsky_funcao: Double: republican legitimation (monument) + Estado Novo appropriation (photograph)

title: Monumento à República, Praça da República, Belém (vista geral)
creator: Unknown (Getúlio Vargas visit album)
description: Full view of Monument to the Republic with female allegorical figure atop a column in Praça da República, Belém. The towering female figure dominates the urban landscape, arms raised, embodying the Republic.
citation_abnt: MONUMENTO à República, Praça da República, Belém. 1940. 1 fotografia, p&b. In: Álbum de fotografias da visita de Getúlio Vargas a Belém. Museu da República/IBRAM. Disponível em: https://brasilianafotografica.bn.gov.br/brasiliana/handle/20.500.12156.1/13611.
panofsky_pre: B&W photo, general view, Republic monument Belém atop column. Tropical trees surround. Same Vargas album.
panofsky_funcao: Territorial normalization — Republic reaches Amazonia

title: Jardim do Campo da Aclamação (Campo de Santana): estátuas do Outono e da Primavera
creator: Guilherme Santos (photographer)
motif_str: Alegoria feminina, Estações, Escultura, Jardim público
description: Sepia photograph showing female allegorical statues representing the seasons of Autumn and Spring in Campo de Santana (formerly Campo da Aclamação), Rio de Janeiro. Female figures as seasonal allegories in a republican public space — note the location at Praça da República.
citation_abnt: SANTOS, Guilherme. Jardim do Campo da Aclamação, atual Campo de Santana; estátuas do Outono e da Primavera. c. 1925. 1 fotografia, gelatina/prata, sépia, 4,5 x 11 cm. Instituto Moreira Salles. Disponível em: https://brasilianafotografica.bn.gov.br/brasiliana/handle/20.500.12156.1/11529.
panofsky_pre: Sepia stereoscopic photo, two female statues (Autumn/Spring) in Campo de Santana garden, Rio. Tropical vegetation.
panofsky_funcao: Ornamental civicization — import European garden culture to tropics

title: Alegoria da República (Décio Villares)
creator: Décio Villares (1851–1931)
source_archive: NYU Faculty Digital Archive / Brasiliana Museus
motif_str: República, Alegoria feminina, Positivismo, Barrete frígio
description: Allegorical painting of the Brazilian Republic by Décio Villares, the positivist artist who designed the blue disc on Brazil's national flag. The female figure wears a Phrygian cap inscribed with 'Ordem e Progresso' — directly linking republican feminine allegory to positivist ideology. Key work for understanding how European allegorical forms were transplanted and adapted in Brazilian republican iconography.
citation_abnt: VILLARES, Décio. Alegoria da República. c. 1900. 1 pintura, óleo sobre tela, 97 x 77 cm. Museu Histórico Nacional. Disponível em: https://archive.nyu.edu/handle/2451/61396.
panofsky_pre: Oil sketch (97x77cm). Female half-body, Phrygian cap inscribed 'Ordem e Progresso'. Serene face, forward gaze. Warm tones, broad brushwork.
panofsky_funcao: Found the visual face of the Brazilian Republic. Positivist program disputed with jacobins.

title: Alegoria da República (Carlos Chambelland)
creator: Carlos Chambelland
description: Allegorical painting commissioned for Brazil's centennial of independence (1922). Female figure in flowing white and green robes, arm raised, accompanied by an angel, with male figures holding manuscripts below — blending republican allegory with national celebration.
citation_abnt: CHAMBELLAND, Carlos. Alegoria da República. 1922. 1 pintura, óleo sobre tela, 202 x 152 cm. Museu Histórico Nacional. Disponível em: https://brasiliana.museus.gov.br/acervos/alegoria-da-republica/.
panofsky_pre: Large oil painting (202x152cm). Female figure, raised arm, white tunic + green mantle (national colors). Angel figure. Male figures with manuscripts below.
panofsky_funcao: Centennial celebration and refoundation (1922)

title: As Estátuas Fallando (The Statues Speaking) — Justiça
creator: Unknown (periodical 'BRASIL')
motif_str: Justiça, Estátua falante, Diálogo alegórico, Verdade
description: Article titled 'As Estátuas Fallando' (The Statues Speaking) featuring a literary dialogue where Justice appears as an animated statue character. 'A Verdade: Que dizes, ó Justiça?' (Truth: What do you say, oh Justice?). Early Brazilian example of Justice personified as a speaking female figure in periodical press.
citation_abnt: AS ESTÁTUAS fallando. Brasil, n. 60, 1827. p. [s.n.]. Disponível em: http://memoria.bn.br/pdf/702390/per702390_1827_00060.pdf.
panofsky_pre: TEXTUAL item — no image. Literary dialogue in periodical 'Brasil' (1827). Justice and Truth as speaking statues (prosopopeia).
panofsky_funcao: Legitimation of imperial juridical order 5 years post-independence

title: Estátua da Justiça (Luiz Rochet) — referência no Almanak Laemmert
creator: Luiz Rochet (sculptor); Almanak Laemmert (source)
motif_str: Justiça, Estátua, Escultor francês, Praça pública
description: Reference in the Almanak Laemmert (1929 edition) to the statue of Justice by French sculptor Luiz Rochet, inaugurated September 1872. Alongside statues of History, Poetry and Science. Documents the importation of French allegorical sculpture into Brazilian public space.
citation_abnt: ALMANAK Laemmert. Rio de Janeiro, 1929. ed. A00085, p. 542. Disponível em: http://memoria.bn.br/docreader/webindex/WIPagina/313394/101306.
panofsky_pre: TEXTUAL reference — Almanak Laemmert (1929) recording Rochet's Justiça sculpture (1872) at Pedro I monument, Rio.
panofsky_funcao: Imperial legitimation through French monumental vocabulary

title: La Justice, la Vengeance et la Vérité
creator: François-Nicolas Chifflart
description: Engraving depicting three female allegorical figures: Justice, Vengeance, and Truth. A powerful composition showing Justice as a dominant female presence, flanked by Truth and divine Vengeance — key triad in French republican allegorical vocabulary.
citation_abnt: CHIFFLART, François-Nicolas. La Justice, la Vengeance et la Vérité. 1865. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b531737635.
panofsky_pre: Three female figures in dynamic aerial flight swooping toward 3-4 grotesque male figures cowering on rocky ground. Classical robes billowing. Lead female extends arm in accusatory pursuit. Mountainous landscape. Etching, monochrome, signed 'F. Chifflart'.
panofsky_funcao: Legitimation of punitive justice through divine feminine agency

title: Le triomphe de la Justice et de la Vérité
creator: François-Nicolas Chifflart
description: Engraving showing the triumph of Justice and Truth as female allegorical figures. Complete state with full lettering. Part of Chifflart's series on juridical allegory.
citation_abnt: CHIFFLART, François-Nicolas. Le triomphe de la Justice et de la Vérité. 1865. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b531737529.
panofsky_pre: Female figure atop cubic pedestal, semi-nude with classical drapery, holding scales. Wing/billowing drapery behind. 4-5 nude male caryatids supporting pedestal. Crowd at base. Rocky promontory. Signed 'F. Chifflart'.
panofsky_funcao: Architectonic legitimation — Justice as capstone of social order supported by male labor

title: L'envoyé de la Justice
creator: François-Nicolas Chifflart
description: Engraving titled 'The Envoy of Justice' — depicting a figure sent by Justice (as a female allegorical power). Early example in the series of Justice representations by Chifflart.
citation_abnt: CHIFFLART, François-Nicolas. L'envoyé de la Justice. 1859. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b53173732g.
panofsky_pre: Central MALE winged figure in cruciform pose, nearly nude. Sword and torch. In upper right, luminous FEMALE figure in classical drapery holding torch, 'JUSTICE' inscribed in sky. Fallen figures below. Deep chiaroscuro.
panofsky_funcao: Female principle generates but does not execute justice. State violence by male body authorized by female source

title: Marianne enseignant l'alphabet à des enfants (naïades et Marianne)
creator: Unknown
description: Engravings depicting naiads and Marianne teaching the alphabet to children. Powerful image of the Republic-as-woman as educator — embodying the republican ideal of laïcité and public instruction through a female allegorical figure.
citation_abnt: ESTAMPES représentant des naïades et Marianne enseignant l'alphabet à des enfants. [1859-1910]. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b10574064v.
panofsky_pre: Cyanotype of TWO engravings. LEFT: Nude female with children (naiads), pastoral. RIGHT: Marianne in white robe, radiant crown, olive branch, teaching children before tablet 'LIBERTÉ ÉGALITÉ FRATERNITÉ / CATÉCHISME RÉPUBLICAIN'.
panofsky_funcao: Civic education through maternal-allegorical body. Quasi-religious CATÉCHISME structure

title: La République aimable (Félicien Rops)
creator: Félicien Rops
motif_str: République, Allégorie féminine, Satire, Corps féminin
description: Satirical engraving by Belgian-French artist Félicien Rops depicting 'The Amiable Republic' — a subversive or eroticized representation of the Republic as a woman. Critical for understanding the contested gendered nature of republican allegory and its use in satirical press.
citation_abnt: ROPS, Félicien. La République aimable. 1871. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b531842166.
panofsky_pre: Standing female, hand on hip. Fitted dress with ruffled collar, visible decollete. Diminished Phrygian cap. Shield inscribed 'RES PUBLICA / THIERS / ETAT!'. Ironic smirk. Lorgnette. Drypoint etching. 'Respublica Amabilis. 1871'.
panofsky_funcao: Delegitimation — satirical critique. Allegory used AGAINST the state

title: The French Crisis: Madame La République
creator: Unknown
motif_str: République, Crise, Allégorie féminine, Caricature politique
description: Political cartoon from 1887 showing 'Madame La République' during the French political crisis. The Republic personified as a woman under stress — a key document of how female allegory was deployed during political instability.
citation_abnt: THE FRENCH crisis: Madame La République. 1887. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b8438243t.
panofsky_pre: Political cartoon of 'Madame La République' during a moment of crisis (1887 Boulangist crisis). Caricatural style of Third Republic press. Monochrome engraving. Phrygian cap probable. Textual caption integrated.
panofsky_funcao: Dramatizes institutional fragility through the feminized body politic

title: République Française: 3e Emprunt de la Défense nationale
creator: René Lelong (1871–1933)
motif_str: Marianne, République, Guerre, Défense nationale, Allégorie féminine
description: WWI propaganda poster for the 3rd National Defense loan. Marianne stands triumphantly above soldiers, embodying the Republic rallying her citizens to war. The female allegory mobilized for military propaganda — a critical junction of gender, state power, and visual persuasion.
citation_abnt: LELONG, René. République Française: 3e Emprunt de la Défense nationale. 1917. 1 cartaz. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/9200518/ark__12148_btv1b10051217v.
panofsky_pre: WWI war bond poster (1917, René Lelong). Monumental Marianne in Phrygian cap and tricolor drapery, arm raised, towering above marching poilus. Vertical composition, polychrome lithograph. 'RÉPUBLIQUE FRANÇAISE / 3e EMPRUNT DE LA DÉFENSE NATIONALE'.
panofsky_funcao: State deploys feminized image to command masculine sacrifice. The poster IS a state financial instrument (war bond).

title: La République nous appelle... (Steinlen)
creator: Théophile Alexandre Steinlen (1859–1923)
motif_str: Marianne, République, Appel, Guerre, Allégorie féminine
description: WWI recruitment poster: 'The Republic calls us...' — Marianne as a summoning female figure, calling citizens to arms. Steinlen's powerful composition shows the Republic-as-woman as a quasi-maternal/military figure demanding sacrifice.
citation_abnt: STEINLEN, Théophile Alexandre. La République nous appelle. 1915. 1 litografia. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/9200518/ark__12148_btv1b10510623s.
panofsky_pre: WWI recruitment poster (1915, Steinlen). Dynamic Marianne in Phrygian cap and classical drapery, striding/summoning. Social-realist lithographic style with earth tones and muted reds. 'La République nous appelle...' Soldiers responding below.
panofsky_funcao: Recruitment mobilization through maternal-allegorical authority

title: Buste de la République (Agence Rol)
creator: Agence Rol (photographic agency)
description: Press photograph of a bust sculpture representing the French Republic. Busts of Marianne became ubiquitous in French town halls (mairies) under the Third Republic — the multiplication of the female allegorical form across thousands of civic spaces.
citation_abnt: BUSTE de la République. [s.d.]. 1 fotografia de imprensa. Agence Rol. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/9200518/ark__12148_btv1b6952880n.
panofsky_pre: Press photograph (Agence Rol, early 20th c.) of a sculpted Marianne bust: female from chest up on socle, classical drapery at shoulders, Phrygian cap, idealized generic features. Isolated against neutral background. Monochromatic silver gelatin print. Bust terminates body at chest.
panofsky_funcao: The bust IS the state. Mandated by circular for every commune. The largest serial deployment of a female allegorical form in modern European history.

title: Le hochet de la République (Jean Veber)
creator: Jean Veber (1868–1928)
description: Satirical print 'The Rattle of the Republic' by Jean Veber. The Republic as a woman reduced to a toy or rattle — a critical/ironic commentary on the infantilization or trivialization of republican symbolism through its female form.
citation_abnt: VEBER, Jean. Le hochet de la République. [s.d.]. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/9200518/ark__12148_btv1b8577646g.
panofsky_pre: Satirical print by Jean Veber depicting the Republic as/with a hochet (baby rattle). Caricatural style, likely exaggerated features. Monochrome engraving/lithograph. From Le Rire or L'Assiette au beurre tradition.
panofsky_funcao: Delegitimation through infantilization — republican allegory as empty signifier, a rattle shaken to pacify

title: Thronende Justitia / Allegorie der strafenden Gerechtigkeit
creator: Januarius Zick (painter); Rudolf Schulze-Marburg (photographer)
description: Photograph of a ceiling fresco in Koblenz showing Justitia enthroned — the allegorical female figure of criminal justice. A German example of Justice as a seated female sovereign figure, wielding punitive authority from a throne-like position.
citation_abnt: ZICK, Januarius. Thronende Justitia / Allegorie der strafenden Gerechtigkeit. [séc. XVIII]. Fotografia de Schulze-Marburg, Rudolf, 1943-1944. Zentralinstitut für Kunstgeschichte. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/201/item_IBA5QWMUFFBZOLE2SPIJO5QD2SPIZS6S.
panofsky_pre: Photograph of Koblenz ceiling fresco: Justitia enthroned with sword and scales.
panofsky_funcao: Allegorical legitimation of criminal justice through sovereign female figure

title: Time and Justice Reveal the Truth
creator: Johan Walker
description: Allegorical depiction showing Time and Justice revealing Truth. Belgian example of the Justice-Truth triad where Justice is personified as a woman who, together with Time, unveils Truth — a visual argument for the transparency of law.
citation_abnt: WALKER, Johan. Time and justice reveal the truth. [s.d.]. Royal Institute for Cultural Heritage. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/2048001/AP_10342206.
panofsky_pre: Copperplate engraving (Johan Walker, KIK-IRPA). Time + Justice unveil nude Truth. Multiple dynamic figures, atmospheric space.
panofsky_funcao: Humanist-juridical pedagogy. Teaches, does not command.

title: Justitia (Jacob Matham)
creator: Jacob Matham
description: Print depicting Justitia — the female allegorical figure of Justice with her traditional attributes (scales, sword). By Jacob Matham, a major Dutch engraver, student of Hendrick Goltzius.
citation_abnt: MATHAM, Jacob. Justitia. c. 1600. 1 gravura. Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/89/item_ZCR4KC47OMJN7DRRDFTIWRQS33M7PBN2.
panofsky_pre: Engraving of Justitia with sword and scales by Jacob Matham.
panofsky_funcao: Vocabulary-establishing print dissemination of legal allegory

title: Allegory of Justice (Charles Audran after B.P. Cortona)
creator: Charles Audran (after Pietro da Cortona)
description: Allegorical representation of Justice, engraved by Charles Audran after an invention by Pietro da Cortona (Berrettini). Italian Baroque model of Justice as a female figure — one of the visual templates that circulated across Europe and eventually reached the Americas.
citation_abnt: AUDRAN, Charles. Allegory of Justice. [séc. XVII]. 1 gravura. Casanatense Library. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/446/RML0348941.
panofsky_pre: Engraving of Justice after Pietro da Cortona by Charles Audran.
panofsky_funcao: Baroque dissemination of Italian legal allegorical model

title: Justitia (Hans Kels d. J.)
creator: Hans Kels d. J.
description: Golden gilded relief sculpture depicting Justitia. A Renaissance example of the female allegorical figure of justice rendered in precious materials — connecting legal symbolism to material luxury and sovereign authority.
citation_abnt: KELS, Hans d. J. Justitia. [séc. XVI]. 1 relevo dourado. Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/15502/KK_6068.
panofsky_pre: Gilded relief sculpture of Justitia by Hans Kels d. J.
panofsky_funcao: Renaissance sovereign legitimation via precious material display

title: Justitia, Allegory of Justice (Johann Oswald Harms)
creator: Johann Oswald Harms
description: Drawing depicting Justitia — allegorical female figure of justice with scales and sword. German Baroque representation of the legal feminine allegory.
citation_abnt: HARMS, Johann Oswald. Justitia, allegory of justice. [séc. XVII]. 1 desenho. Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/89/item_MH6IXNHWTECBQCNPU7IIMCFP2BDFAV76.
panofsky_pre: Baroque drawing of Justitia with scales and sword by Harms.
panofsky_funcao: Artistic codification of legal feminine attributes

title: Justitia civilis (Maarten de Vos)
creator: Maarten de Vos
motif_str: Justitia civilis, Justice civile, Allégorie féminine
description: Allegorical depiction of civil justice (Justitia civilis) by Flemish master Maarten de Vos. Distinction between civil and criminal justice personified as separate female figures — important for understanding the multiplication of legal feminine allegories.
citation_abnt: VOS, Maarten de. Justitia civilis. [séc. XVI]. Royal Institute for Cultural Heritage. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/2048001/AP_10133590.
panofsky_pre: Copperplate engraving after Maarten de Vos (KIK-IRPA). Justitia civilis with civil-law attributes. Multi-figural, Mannerist style.
panofsky_funcao: Legal-humanist education. Proto-industrial Antwerp print system generates vocabulary later states adopt.

title: Allegory with Justizia, crowned by a putto
creator: Kaspar Waldmann
description: Allegorical representation of Justizia resting on clouds, being crowned by a putto (cherub), with scales visible. Justice as a celestial female figure receiving divine coronation — the theological dimension of legal allegory.
citation_abnt: WALDMANN, Kaspar. Allegory with Justizia, resting on a cloudbank, crowned by a putto. [séc. XVIII]. 1 desenho. Albertina Museum. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/15508/30435.
panofsky_pre: Drawing of Justitia crowned by putto by Kaspar Waldmann.
panofsky_funcao: Theological sanctification of judicial authority

title: Female Allegory (Pierre Puvis de Chavannes)
creator: Pierre Puvis de Chavannes
description: Female allegorical figure by Pierre Puvis de Chavannes, the great French muralist whose public commissions (Sorbonne, Panthéon, Hôtel de Ville) defined the visual language of Third Republic civic spaces. This drawing connects to the larger programme of republican allegorical decoration.
citation_abnt: PUVIS DE CHAVANNES, Pierre. Female allegory. [séc. XIX]. 1 desenho. Albertina Museum. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/15508/DG1918_7.
panofsky_pre: Drawing of female allegory by Pierre Puvis de Chavannes.
panofsky_funcao: Civic decorative programme for Third Republic institutions

title: Justiça popular (UDP political poster)
creator: União Democrática Popular (UDP)
description: Political poster from the Portuguese revolutionary period (post-Carnation Revolution, 1974): 'Popular Justice: the PIDE agent who murdered Dias Coelho will be judged at the people's cost!' Justice invoked in revolutionary political context — a moment when the concept of Justice was being radically renegotiated.
citation_abnt: UNIÃO DEMOCRÁTICA POPULAR. Justiça popular: o Pide que assassinou Dias Coelho vai ser julgado nas costas do povo! [1975?]. 1 cartaz. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/17148-justica-popular.
panofsky_pre: Political poster 'Justiça popular' (UDP) post-Carnation Revolution.
panofsky_funcao: Revolutionary popular renegotiation of legal authority

title: Alegoria à História (female allegorical engraving)
creator: Unknown
description: Historical allegorical engraving featuring female figures representing History. An early modern Portuguese example of the female allegorical tradition — History personified as a woman, part of the same visual vocabulary that produced Justice and Republic figures.
citation_abnt: [ALEGORIA à História]. c. 1600. 1 gravura, água-forte, p&b. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/39213-alegoria-a-historia.
panofsky_pre: Engraving personifying History as female allegorical figure.
panofsky_funcao: Early modern Portuguese allegorical historiography

title: Alegoria à Morte (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
creator: Pierre Antoine Quillard (1701–1733)
description: Allegorical engraving representing Death, part of a series of allegorical works by the French-Portuguese artist Quillard produced in Lisbon. Demonstrates the French-Portuguese artistic exchange in allegorical visual culture during the Baroque period.
citation_abnt: QUILLARD, Pierre Antoine. Alegoria à Morte. 1730. 1 gravura. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/37491-alegoria-a-morte.
panofsky_pre: Baroque allegorical engraving of Death by Quillard.
panofsky_funcao: Baroque moral-didactic allegorical programme

title: Alegoria ao Tempo (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
creator: Pierre Antoine Quillard (1701–1733)
description: Allegorical engraving representing Time, companion piece to the Alegoria à Morte. Part of Quillard's allegorical series produced in Lisbon. Time as a personified figure — part of the broader iconographic programme where abstract concepts (Justice, Time, Truth, Death) take human form.
citation_abnt: QUILLARD, Pierre Antoine. Alegoria ao Tempo. 1730. 1 gravura. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/37507-alegoria-ao-tempo.
panofsky_pre: Baroque allegorical engraving of Time by Quillard.
panofsky_funcao: Temporal allegorical framing of human and legal affairs

title: A Republica precisa de ti: vota em Norton de Matos
creator: Comissão Distrital do Porto da Candidatura
motif_str: República, Alegoria feminina, Eleição, Cartaz político
description: Electoral poster from the 1949 Portuguese presidential campaign featuring a female allegorical figure representing the Portuguese Republic. 'The Republic needs you: vote for Norton de Matos.' A classical female figure in robes symbolizes the Republic during a period of authoritarian governance — the allegory deployed as opposition to dictatorship.
citation_abnt: A REPUBLICA precisa de ti: vota em Norton de Matos. 1949. 1 cartaz. Comissão Distrital do Porto. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/.
panofsky_pre: Electoral poster featuring Republic allegory (Norton de Matos 1949).
panofsky_funcao: Democratic mobilization against authoritarian regime

title: Illustrations de Calendrier et compost des bergiers (Danse macabre — female Justice figure)
creator: Anonymous
motif_str: Justice, Danse macabre, Figure féminine, Manuscrit
description: Illustrations from the 'Calendar and Almanac of Shepherds' featuring the dance of death and allegorical figures including Justice. An early representation of Justice as a female figure within the memento mori tradition — the intersection of death, morality, and law.
citation_abnt: CALENDRIER et compost des bergiers: La grant danse macabre. 1531. Manuscrito ilustrado. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/.
panofsky_pre: Illustrated manuscript: Justice in Danse macabre tradition.
panofsky_funcao: Late medieval memento mori integration with justice

title: Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen mit Plastik der Justitia (Hans Gieng, 1543)
creator: Hans Gieng (sculptor)
description: The Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen (Fountain of Justice) in Bern — the first known blindfolded representation of Lady Justice (1543). Hans Gieng's statue holds sword and scales, blindfolded, standing atop vanquished figures representing worldly power (pope, sultan, emperor, magistrate). A foundational image in the history of legal iconography.
citation_abnt: GIENG, Hans. Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen mit Plastik der Justitia. 1543. 1 escultura, fonte. Bern, Gerechtigkeitsgasse. Bildarchiv Foto Marburg. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/que20183316.
panofsky_pre: Polychrome stone sculpture atop octagonal Renaissance fountain column in Bern. Female figure in contrapposto, blindfolded, raising sword and holding scales. Long flowing dress, crowned. Four smaller figures beneath representing pope, sultan, emperor, magistrate.
panofsky_regime: Foundational Contrato Sexual Visual: female body embodies Ju
panofsky_funcao: Civic fountain establishing visible public authority in municipal space

title: Justitia (marble head from Porta di Capua)
creator: Unknown (Hohenstaufen workshop)
description: Marble head of Justitia from the Porta di Capua, built under Emperor Frederick II. One of the earliest surviving medieval personifications of Justice as a woman — predating the Renaissance tradition. Connected to the Hohenstaufen revival of Roman legal imagery.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA (cabeça em mármore da Porta di Capua). 1239–1240. 1 escultura em mármore. Museo Provinciale Campano, Capua. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj08148970.
panofsky_pre: Over-life-size marble head of a woman, white marble weathered to grey-cream. Classicizing features: straight nose, smooth brow, serene expression, almond-shaped eyes. Hair centrally parted in Roman matron style. Fragment — sole surviving portion of larger figure. No attributes preserved.
panofsky_regime: Foundational Contrato Sexual Visual: gendering of legal auth
panofsky_funcao: Imperial Hohenstaufen revival of Roman judicial authority

title: Die Göttin der Gerechtigkeit nach dem heutigen Geschmacke
creator: Bernhard Rode
description: The Goddess of Justice according to contemporary taste' — an Enlightenment-era satirical engraving critiquing contemporary justice through its female allegorical form. Shows how the figure of Justice was deployed as a vehicle for political commentary.
citation_abnt: RODE, Bernhard. Die Göttin der Gerechtigkeit nach dem heutigen Geschmacke. Século XVIII. 1 gravura. Kupferstich-Kabinett Dresden. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj30110594.
panofsky_pre: Monochromatic copper engraving depicting female figure as Goddess of Justice. Title signals satirical intent. Rode's Enlightenment-era graphic style with hatching/cross-hatching. Classical drapery and Justitia attributes deployed with deliberate irony.
panofsky_regime: Enlightenment allegorical self-reflexivity. Rode's satire ex
panofsky_funcao: Enlightenment satirical critique of judicial corruption

title: Justitia an der Rathausuhr (Esslingen)
creator: Unknown
description: Justitia figure on the town hall clock of Esslingen am Neckar (1589). Justice as a permanent civic presence on a public timepiece — marking the hours under the gaze of the female allegory of law.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA an der Rathausuhr, Esslingen am Neckar. 1589. 1 escultura. Altes Rathaus, Esslingen. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20553978.
panofsky_pre: Female standing figure mounted on facade of civic building as part of clock ensemble. Upright, frontal, holding sword and scales. Long draped robe. Positioned within architectural niche on the Altes Rathaus of Esslingen am Neckar (1589). Painted stone or wood.
panofsky_regime: Paradigmatic Feminilidade de Estado in fundacional mode. Fem
panofsky_funcao: Temporal regulation of civic order under perpetual justice gaze

title: Barocke Holzdecke: Personifikation der Gerechtigkeit
creator: Unknown
description: Baroque wooden ceiling in a Lüneburg residential building with allegorical medallions: Personification of Justice. The female justice figure domesticated — appearing not only in courts and public buildings but in private domestic spaces.
citation_abnt: PERSONIFIKATION der Gerechtigkeit (Barocke Holzdecke). 1660–1780. 1 medalhão em teto de madeira. Lüneburg, Große Bäckerstraße 12. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20672587.
panofsky_pre: Painted or carved medallion (tondo) in Baroque wooden coffered ceiling, Luneburg residential building. Single female figure within circular frame, holding sword/scales. Warm polychrome palette, soft drapery, dynamic pose within tondo format.
panofsky_regime: Pre-statist Nachleben of legal allegory. Justitia in domesti
panofsky_funcao: Domestic integration of judicial virtue into patrician home

title: Allegorie: Justitia (Marcantonio Raimondi)
creator: Marcantonio Raimondi
description: Engraving of Justitia by Marcantonio Raimondi, the most important Italian engraver of the High Renaissance (pupil of Raphael's circle). This print disseminated the Italian Renaissance model of female Justice across Europe.
citation_abnt: RAIMONDI, Marcantonio. Allegorie: Justitia. Início do século XVI. 1 gravura. Bibliotheca Hertziana, Roma. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj08158050.
panofsky_pre: Standing female figure in classical draped garments, black-and-white engraving with fine crosshatching. Contrapposto stance, holding sword and scales. Raphaelesque ideal: idealized classical proportions visible beneath flowing drapery. Minimal background.
panofsky_regime: Pivotal Nachleben position: Raimondi as mediator between pap
panofsky_funcao: Dissemination of High Renaissance classical judicial ideal

title: Allegorie der Justitia und eine weitere weibliche Allegorie
creator: Unknown (Italian)
description: Italian drawing or print showing Justitia alongside another female allegorical figure. Early 16th-century example of the pairing of Justice with other virtues (Prudence, Temperance, Fortitude) — the four cardinal virtues personified as women.
citation_abnt: ALLEGORIE der Justitia und eine weitere weibliche Allegorie. 1501–1550. 1 desenho/gravura. Museo Civico, Bassano del Grappa. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj08108743.
panofsky_pre: Drawing or print on paper: two standing female figures in classical drapery. Monochrome ink (pen/wash or engraving). Contrapposto poses, flowing robes. One holds sword/scales (Justice), companion holds mirror/serpent (Prudence). Simple composition, no elaborate setting.
panofsky_regime: Foundational regime: femininity mobilized to render legal au
panofsky_funcao: Ethical balancing of Justice with Prudence as cardinal virtue

title: Justitia (Hameln, Stiftsherrenhaus)
creator: Unknown
description: Justitia figure on the Stiftsherrenhaus (Canon's House) in Hamelin, c. 1558. A Weser Renaissance example of Justice as architectural ornament on a residential/ecclesiastical building.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA (Stiftsherrenhaus, Hameln). c. 1558. 1 escultura arquitetônica. Hameln, Osterstraße 8. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20608421.
panofsky_pre: Sandstone relief figure on multi-storey facade. Female figure in architectural niche, wearing layered classicizing drapery. Holds sword and scales. Frontal, erect posture. Weathered Obernkirchener sandstone, monochromatic grey-buff. Flanked by Weser Renaissance ornamental framing.
panofsky_regime: Feminilidade de Estado at local pre-national level. Female b
panofsky_funcao: Weser Renaissance civic decoration sanctifying urban law

title: Relief: Gerechtigkeit und Eintracht (Bremen Rathaus)
creator: Unknown
description: Relief of Justice (Gerechtigkeit) and Concord (Eintracht) on the Bremen Old Town Hall (1596–1605). Female Justice paired with female Concord on a civic building — the visual argument that justice produces social harmony.
citation_abnt: RELIEF: Gerechtigkeit und Eintracht. 1596–1605. 1 relevo. Altes Rathaus, Bremen. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20459153.
panofsky_pre: Two female figures in stone relief on Bremen Altes Rathaus facade. Justice holds sword and scales; Concord holds cornucopia/bundle. Shallow-to-moderate depth relief, integrated into architectural surface. Monochrome stone, frontal arrangement within architectonic framing.
panofsky_regime: Foundational Contrato Sexual Visual in municipal form. Femal
panofsky_funcao: Municipal civic harmony derived from justice and concord

title: Allegorie der Jus Civile (Christian Wenzinger)
creator: Christian Wenzinger
description: Allegory of Civil Law (Jus Civile) by Christian Wenzinger, 1752, at a former Benedictine abbey. Distinction between civil and canonical law personified — Justice in her specifically secular legal form within an ecclesiastical setting.
citation_abnt: WENZINGER, Christian. Allegorie der Jus Civile. 1752. 1 escultura. Sankt Peter, Benedictine Abbey. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20677105.
panofsky_pre: Full-length female figure in polychromed limewood, Rococo contrapposto with S-curve and flowing drapery. Placed in niche/console within Benedictine abbey library of Sankt Peter im Schwarzwald. Dynamic pose, deep drapery undercuts, polychrome. Attributes include codex of civil law.
panofsky_regime: Female body as epistemological container for civil/canon law
panofsky_funcao: Ecclesiastical codification of civil law virtue

title: Kamin mit Justitia (Leipzig, Altes Rathaus)
creator: Unknown
description: Fireplace with Justitia in the Leipzig Old Town Hall (c. 1610). Justice as a decorative element on a fireplace in the main council chamber — the warming presence of legal authority in the deliberative space.
citation_abnt: KAMIN mit Justitia (Leipzig, Altes Rathaus). c. 1610. 1 decoração de lareira. Altes Rathaus, Leipzig. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj30143134.
panofsky_pre: Fireplace relief with Justitia in Leipzig Old Town Hall council room.
panofsky_funcao: Civic deliberative sanctification in town hall interior

title: Vrouwe Justitia (nude, with sword and scales)
creator: Anonymous
motif_str: Justitia, Justice, nude allegory, sword, scales
description: 16th-century engraving of Vrouwe Justitia — nude, holding sword in right hand, scales at left, appearing to trample a child underfoot. A muscular, powerful rendering of female Justice — far from the idealized classical model.
citation_abnt: VROUWE Justitia (nua, com espada e balança). 1500–1600. 1 gravura. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/object/Vrouwe-Justitia--13997b5b276f9bbbb36a847da4c3022a.
panofsky_pre: Engraving of Vrouwe Justitia (nude, sword and scales).
panofsky_funcao: Northern Renaissance muscular personification of judicial force

title: Justitia (bust with crown and eye pendant)
creator: Unknown
description: Bust of a woman with a crown and a necklace bearing an eye pendant, identified in inscription as Justitia. The all-seeing eye as a Justice attribute — surveillance and omniscience as female qualities of law.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA (busto com coroa e olho pendente). [s.d.]. 1 escultura (busto). Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/object/Justitia--314f580f935ba978fb199ce7abeb0db1.
panofsky_pre: Bust sculpture of Justitia with crown and eye pendant.
panofsky_funcao: Institutional surveillance and all-seeing vigilance

title: Allegorie op de rechtvaardigheid (Allegory of Justice, enthroned)
creator: Unknown
motif_str: Justitia, Justice, enthroned, sovereignty of law
description: Title page with enthroned Justice (Rechtvaardigheid) on a pedestal. At her feet, attributes symbolizing worldly power. The throne-composition as a visual argument for the sovereignty of law over political authority.
citation_abnt: ALLEGORIE op de rechtvaardigheid. Século XVII. 1 gravura (página de título). Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/object/Allegorie-op-de-rechtvaardigheid--a26144337b14ab57eb5ca23025308032.
panofsky_pre: Title page engraving of enthroned Justice on pedestal.
panofsky_funcao: Frontispiece legitimation of printed legal authority

title: Justitia enthroned, with sword and scales
creator: Unknown
motif_str: Justitia, Justice, enthroned, sword, scales, putti
description: Interior with Justitia enthroned, holding a sword and scales; female allegorical figures looking up to her and two putti holding shields. A formal composition of Justice as sovereign female judge.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA enthroned, with sword and scales. Século XVII. 1 gravura. British Museum, London. Disponível em: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/P_1870-0625-185.
panofsky_pre: Engraving: Justitia enthroned with sword and scales. Secondary female figures look up. Putti hold shields. Baroque, monochrome.
panofsky_funcao: Feminilidade de Estado in early modern form

title: Providence and Justice (female personifications in niches)
creator: Unknown
description: Providence and Justice, female personifications, whole-length, in niches, with attributes (ruler and scales, snake entwined around arm). Justice paired with Providence in architectural niches — the virtues as guardians of civic space.
citation_abnt: PROVIDENCE and Justice (personificações femininas em nichos). [s.d.]. 1 gravura. British Museum, London. Disponível em: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/P_1862-0712-304.
panofsky_pre: Two female figures in architectural niches. Providence (ruler+scales) and Justice (snake). Frontal, symmetrical, monochrome engraving.
panofsky_funcao: Female body as moral infrastructure of institutions

title: Justitia and Prudentia (female personifications)
creator: Unknown
motif_str: Justitia, Justice, Prudentia, sword, mirror, cardinal virtues
description: Justice and Prudence, female personifications, whole-length, in niches, with attributes (sword and tablets of the law; mirror and snake). The cardinal-virtue pairing of Justice and Prudence as women.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA and Prudentia (personificações femininas). [s.d.]. 1 gravura. British Museum, London. Disponível em: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/P_1862-0712-305.
panofsky_pre: Companion to UK-002. Justitia (sword+tablets) and Prudentia (mirror+snake) in niches. Same format.
panofsky_funcao: Tablets of law shift from distributive to positive justice

title: America pois'd in the balance of justice
creator: Unknown
description: Revolutionary-era print showing two despondent women (possibly Britannia and America) in a rugged landscape, with ships and a burning city. The balance of justice as a geopolitical metaphor during the American Revolution.
citation_abnt: AMERICA pois'd in the balance of justice. 1776. 1 gravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2004673327/.
panofsky_pre: Etching: two despondent female figures in desolate landscape. Ships, burning city background. Scales (balance) as central motif. Melancholic, turbulent.
panofsky_funcao: Allegorical narration of founding crisis — rupture between Britain and colonies

title: Justice and History (plaster model for US Capitol)
creator: Thomas Crawford (sculptor); John Wood (photographer)
medium: Salted paper print of sculpture maquette
description: Photograph of plaster model for 'Justice and History' by Thomas Crawford, designed for the Senate bronze doors at the East Portico of the US Capitol. Justice and History as paired female figures guarding the entrance to the legislative chamber.
citation_abnt: CRAWFORD, Thomas. Justice and History (modelo para o Capitólio dos EUA). c. 1860. 1 fotografia (salt print). Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2009631377/.
panofsky_pre: Photo of plaster sculptural group: two standing females in heavy classical drapery. Static, symmetrical. Designed for Capitol tympanum.
panofsky_funcao: Female body as threshold guardian of sacred legislative space

title: Justice (blindfolded woman with sword and scales)
creator: US Bureau of Printing & Engraving
description: Official US government steel engraving of blindfolded Justice holding sword and scales. An institutional production of the legal allegory — the state manufacturing its own symbolic self-representation.
citation_abnt: JUSTICE (mulher vendada com espada e balança). [s.d.]. 1 gravura em aço. US Bureau of Printing & Engraving. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2007675578/.
panofsky_pre: Steel engraving: single blindfolded female, sword raised, scales balanced. Minimal background. Bureau of Engraving quality.
panofsky_funcao: Serial bureaucratic legitimation — authenticates and normalizes

title: Foire France-Américaine: Justice, Liberty, Demeter, Athena
creator: Maurice Romberg
motif_str: Justice, Liberty, Athena, Demeter, Marianne, Columbia
description: WWI-era Franco-American poster showing four allegorical figures: Justice, Liberty (with American flag), Demeter, and Athena above Saint-Sulpice. The transatlantic circulation of female legal allegories during wartime.
citation_abnt: ROMBERG, Maurice. Foire France-Américaine: Justice, Liberty, Demeter, Athena. 1917. 1 litogravura colorida. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/99613542/.
panofsky_pre: Color lithograph poster. Four female allegories (Justice, Liberty, Demeter, Athena) floating above Place Saint-Sulpice, Paris. Art Nouveau style, warm saturated palette.
panofsky_funcao: Wartime fundraising through allegorical spectacle

title: Behold! a fabric now to freedom rear'd (Constitutional allegory)
creator: James Trenchard
description: Allegorical scene celebrating the US Constitution: Concord standing, Clio writing, Cupid holding the 'Constitution' before a pillar labeled 'Sacred to Liberty Justice and Peace' with thirteen columns. Female allegories deployed to sanctify the constitutional founding.
citation_abnt: TRENCHARD, James. Behold! a fabric now to freedom rear'd. 1788. 1 gravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2004676797/.
panofsky_pre: Etching: complex constitutional founding tableau. Concord (central), Clio (writing), Cupid (holding Constitution). 13 columns = 13 states. 'Sacred to Liberty Justice and Peace'.
panofsky_funcao: Sacralization of constitutional ratification through female allegorical bodies

title: Die Wage der Macht / La balance de la puissance
creator: Johann Martin Will
description: Justice holding scales on which Britannia outweighs a Spaniard, Frenchman, America (as Native), and Dutchman. Justice as a geopolitical arbiter — weighing national power through the female allegorical figure. Bilingual (German/French) print.
citation_abnt: WILL, Johann Martin. Die Wage der Macht / La balance de la puissance. 1780. 1 gravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2004673370/.
panofsky_pre: Etching: central female with large scales. Britannia on one side, Spain/France/America/Netherlands on other. Bilingual German/French. Augsburg.
panofsky_funcao: Geopolitical argumentation: female body IS the argument — scales are body extended into political space

title: Columbia presenting sword to Admiral Dewey
creator: Unknown
description: Columbia, the female personification of America, presenting a sword and crowning Admiral Dewey after the Spanish-American War. The martial dimension of the national female allegory — Columbia as warrior-queen bestowing military honors.
citation_abnt: COLUMBIA presenting sword to Admiral Dewey. 1899. 1 cromolitogravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2018697020/.
panofsky_pre: Chromolithograph: Columbia in flag-colored robes presenting sword to uniformed Admiral Dewey. Patriotic background. Popular mass-market style.
panofsky_funcao: Imperial legitimation through feminine investiture. Domesticates imperialism via mass-market print.

title: Hedwig Reicher as Columbia in suffrage pageant
creator: Unknown (photograph)
description: German actress Hedwig Reicher in costume as 'Columbia' at a suffrage pageant where Columbia summoned Justice, Charity, Liberty, Peace, and Hope to revive the crusade of women. A feminist reappropriation of national female allegory — Columbia mobilized for women's suffrage.
citation_abnt: HEDWIG Reicher as Columbia in suffrage pageant. 1913. 1 fotografia. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/97510759/.
panofsky_pre: B&W photograph: Hedwig Reicher (actress) in Columbia costume on Treasury Building steps. Star-spangled diadem, white classical robes. Suffrage pageant March 3, 1913.
panofsky_funcao: Reappropriation: Columbia, used 130 years to mask women's exclusion, is seized BY women to demand inclusion

title: The Goddess of Liberty (woman in star-spangled cape)
creator: Unknown
description: Photograph of a woman model in Liberty costume with stars, representing Liberty/Columbia during the Civil War era. The living body performing the allegory — a real woman embodying the national feminine symbol.
citation_abnt: THE GODDESS of Liberty (mulher com capa estrelada). 1861. 1 fotografia (carte de visite). Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2018664118/.
panofsky_pre: Carte de visite photo: real woman in star-spangled cape as Liberty/Columbia. Studio setting, Civil War era.
panofsky_funcao: Everyday patriotic circulation of allegorical female body

title: Gerechtigkeit (Allegory of Justice) by Lucas Cranach the Elder
creator: Lucas Cranach the Elder
motif_str: Justitia, Justice, nude allegory, sword, scales
description: Painting showing the personification of Justice as a half-length nude female figure against dark background, holding sword and scales. Inscribed 'GERECHTIGKAEIT'. One of the most influential Renaissance depictions — Cranach's eroticized Justice figure set a visual template that persisted for centuries. Northern Renaissance.
citation_abnt: CRANACH, Lucas, o Velho. Gerechtigkeit. 1537. 1 pintura, óleo sobre painel, 72 × 49,6 cm. Coleção particular. Disponível em: https://lucascranach.org/en/PRIVATE_NONE-P457/.
panofsky_pre: Painting of Gerechtigkeit by Lucas Cranach the Elder (1537).
panofsky_funcao: Northern Renaissance humanistic-eroticized legal template

title: La Liberté guidant le peuple (Eugène Delacroix)
creator: Eugène Delacroix
description: Liberty Leading the People' — the iconic image of the July Revolution of 1830. A bare-breasted female figure (Liberty/Marianne) leads armed citizens over barricades, holding the tricolour flag and a musket. The most powerful visual crystallization of the republic-as-woman — Warner's central case study, Agulhon's key image. Foundational for the entire Iconocracy project.
citation_abnt: DELACROIX, Eugène. La Liberté guidant le peuple. 1830. 1 pintura, óleo sobre tela, 260 × 325 cm. Musée du Louvre, Paris. Disponível em: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Eug%C3%A8ne_Delacroix_-_Le_28_Juillet._La_Libert%C3%A9_guidant_le_peuple.jpg.
panofsky_pre: Delacroix, Liberty Leading the People (1830 oil on canvas).
panofsky_funcao: Foundational revolutionary mobilization through romantic feminine allegory

title: Lady Justice (F.W. Pomeroy, Old Bailey, London)
creator: Frederick William Pomeroy
motif_str: Justice, Lady Justice, sword, scales, unblindfolded
description: The iconic gold statue of Lady Justice atop the Old Bailey, London's Central Criminal Court. Notably unblindfolded — holding sword and scales, with spiked crown. The courthouse brochures explain that 'her maidenly form is supposed to guarantee her impartiality.' A prime example of how the female body itself is argued to embody legal virtue.
citation_abnt: POMEROY, Frederick William. Lady Justice. 1907. 1 escultura em bronze dourado. Central Criminal Court (Old Bailey), London. Disponível em: http://www.speel.me.uk/sculptlondon/oldbaileyjustice.htm.
panofsky_pre: Gilt bronze, 3.7m, atop Old Bailey dome at 60m. Sword raised, scales balanced. NO BLINDFOLD. Spiked crown. Gold on sky. Inaugurated 1907 by Edward VII.
panofsky_funcao: State criminal justice made visible and inescapable from across London

title: A Justiça (Alfredo Ceschiatti, STF Brasília)
creator: Alfredo Ceschiatti
motif_str: Justiça, Justice, Themis, blindfold, sword, modernism
description: Monumental granite sculpture of Justice (Themis) seated before the Supreme Federal Tribunal in Brasília. Eyes closed, holding a sword with both hands. Designed to complement Oscar Niemeyer's modernist architecture. The Brazilian Justiça — a seated, blindfolded, sword-bearing woman as the face of the highest court. Attacked on January 8, 2023, making it a central object in the dissertation's analysis of iconoclasm and legal literacy.
citation_abnt: CESCHIATTI, Alfredo. A Justiça. 1961. 1 escultura em granito. Supremo Tribunal Federal, Praça dos Três Poderes, Brasília. Disponível em: https://acervos.ims.com.br/index.php/Detail/objects/18758.
panofsky_pre: Monumental seated female in grey granite, ~3.3m, before the STF in Brasilia. Seated on cubic block, eyes closed (not blindfolded — modernist abstraction), both hands grip vertical sword pointing down. No scales. Simplified classical drapery. Framed by Niemeyer's glass-marble STF building. Reflecting pool.
panofsky_funcao: Monumentalize Justice as silent, blind, armed authority. Inaugurated 1961 (Kubitschek) but served military regime 1964-1985.

title: Allégorie de la Justice (Joseph Stallaert, Brussels City Hall)
creator: Joseph Stallaert
description: Allegorical painting of Justice in the Mayor's Cabinet of Brussels City Hall, by Joseph Stallaert. Part of a triptych with Charity and Foresight — three female allegorical virtues required of a mayor. Justice symbolized by scales and sword. A Belgian civic example connecting female virtue to political authority.
citation_abnt: STALLAERT, Joseph. Allégorie de la Justice. 1885–1888. 1 pintura (teto). Hôtel de Ville, Bruxelles. Disponível em: https://collections.heritage.brussels/fr/objects/36822.
panofsky_pre: Ceiling painting, Mayor's Cabinet, Brussels City Hall. Justice with scales and sword, flanked by Charity and Foresight. Academic naturalist, polychromatic.
panofsky_funcao: Civic legitimation through virtue allegory. Feminine virtues guide male municipal authority.

title: Eliseu Visconti — Alegoria (Biblioteca Nacional, Rio de Janeiro)
creator: Eliseu Visconti
description: Impressionist-style allegorical panel for the Presidential Room of the Biblioteca Nacional in Rio de Janeiro. Female allegorical figure in Visconti's distinctive impressionist idiom — the French-trained Brazilian artist adapting European allegorical vocabulary to national institutional decoration. A key example of transatlantic visual transfer.
citation_abnt: VISCONTI, Eliseu. Alegoria (Biblioteca Nacional). 1910. 1 painel decorativo, óleo. Fundação Biblioteca Nacional, Rio de Janeiro. Disponível em: https://eliseuvisconti.com.br/obra/d702/.
panofsky_pre: Large decorative oil panel, Biblioteca Nacional Rio de Janeiro. Female figure in Visconti's impressionist-symbolist idiom: warm golds, pinks, blues. Soft atmospheric brushwork, dissolved contours. Corporeal, sensuous, draped in flowing fabrics revealing body beneath.
panofsky_funcao: Decorative legitimation of republican cultural apparatus. Belle Epoque Rio.

title: Palais de Justice de Bruxelles (Joseph Poelaert)
creator: Joseph Poelaert (architect)
motif_str: Justice, classical allegory, civic architecture, colonialism
description: The Brussels Palace of Justice — one of the largest courthouses ever built and a monument to 19th-century legal grandeur. The 'pompous staircase with sculptures attired in Roman robes' and allegorical female figures throughout. Poelaert's design made the Belgian state visible through classical feminine allegory. Central to the dissertation's Belgian case study and Huygebaert's colonial paternalism analysis.
citation_abnt: POELAERT, Joseph. Palais de Justice de Bruxelles. 1866–1883. Complexo arquitetônico. Bruxelles. Disponível em: https://be-monumen.be/patrimoine-belge/poelaert-joseph/.
panofsky_pre: Largest courthouse in the world (26,000m2, 104m dome). Assyro-Greco-Roman eclectic in Belgian bluestone/limestone. Colossal Themis/Minerva bust crowning portico. Caryatid figures at base. Interior: male jurists only (Demosthenes, Lycurgus, Cicero, Ulpian). All monochromatic stone.
panofsky_funcao: State self-legitimation through architectural overwhelm. Citizens must ascend monumental staircase — physical submission to legal authority.

title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
